text:
samir: Heads-up — EU customer on Private wants direct SIEM ingestion + their HSM for KMS (PKCS#11). Also got a vuln scan flagging openssl in our onprem runtime. Need plan and owners.

maria: Do we have the SIEM protocol details? TCP514 vs TLS syslog? PKCS#11 support exists in docs but not in our default private package.

samir: They want TLS Syslog over TCP/6514 to a gateway in their peered VPC, with strict mTLS. Scan excerpt attached (summary): openssl 1.1.1c -> CVE medium, shows up in base image used by onprem appliance.

aj: Quick notes: do NOT open broad egress. Suggest: egress NAT + allowlist to the gateway IPs, per-namespace NetworkPolicy for the logging sidecar, and kube-proxy conntrack tuning.

liz: Compliance will need a key-residency attestation and audit log chain-of-custody. We'll need a simple artifact template to hand to the customer.

security-oncall: Triage checklist: 1) Confirm whether vulnerable openssl is in runtime or just build-time packages. 2) If runtime, prioritize patch in staging + canary. 3) Enable auditd + remote log forwarding (to their SIEM or our temporary protected bucket) while patching. 4) Capture forensic snapshot if process exposed.

ops: +1. Runbook reference: https://intranet.redwood/example-runbooks/onprem-security-hardening (see steps 4-7 for SIEM integration).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: ticket INF-2345 created for openssl upgrade in staging and canary clusters.

jordan: I can take the openssl patch. Need build access to the private appliance image and the Dockerfile that pulls the base. @maria can you grant?

maria: @jordan granted build access and added you to "private-deploy-build". Also we should sign exported logs using envelope keys from the customer's HSM-backed KMS so they have non-repudiable proof. Sample KMS key policy snippet: 

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "AllowCustomerHSMUse","Effect": "Allow","Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::CUSTOMER:role/HSMIntegration"},"Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Sign"],"Resource": "*"}
  ]
}
```

aj: For NetworkPolicy, start with a minimal ingress rule for the logging namespace and egress allowlist. Example (apply to namespace "logging"):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-siem-egress
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/32 # customer SIEM gateway (placeholder)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6514
```

security-oncall: Also add alerting: if audit log forwarding fails (no logs for 5m) -> Pager duty P0. If envelope signature verification fails -> P1 and block exports.

samir: Proposed schedule: 1) Confirm SIEM IPs & mTLS cert chain from the customer (today). 2) Patch openssl in staging (48h). 3) Deploy networkpolicy + egress allowlist to staging and validate. 4) Test SIEM ingestion and signed logs in staging airgapped test. 5) Roll to canary, then prod during approved change window. Owners: @jordan (patch), @aj (netpol + egress), @maria (KMS policy + audit config).

maria: Acknowledged. I'll draft the attestation artifact and update the Private Deploy runbook. Will add a short checklist for the change window.

ops: I'll carve a change window: Friday 03:00 UTC, 2-hour maintenance. Creating CHG-7890 and will loop in SRE.

samir: Thanks — I'll coordinate certs with the customer and attach the vuln scan full output to INF-2345. Please post validation steps once done. :thumbsup:

security-oncall: One more: capture packet capture inside staging gateway during SIEM test (pcap) and store with restricted access for 90d.

maria: Noted — will add pcap step to the runbook and ensure KMS policy covers access to artifacts.

jordan: Starting on patch now, will post progress in INF-2345.

ops: noted and marking as high priority.
